description: Measured creator-transaction gas, swept across the guardian band at two payload sizes on a 36-guardian devnet (27 July 2026). The SDK declares a model fitted to these points with ~25% headroom; gas-model.test.ts fails if the model ever declares less than a measured point, which is the failure that would put a creator's transaction out of gas. Both phases scale with the band — phase 1 walks the candidate set and freezes one bond per selected guardian, phase 2 carries one share envelope each plus the payload stored once — so neither can be expressed as a flat figure. Re-measure after any change to selection, the secret record, or the share-distribution path; do NOT widen the margin to accommodate a regression.

conditions.registered_guardians: 40 for phase 1 (29 July 2026); 36 for phase 2 and cancel (27 July 2026)
conditions.note: The phase-1 base covers candidate enumeration, which reads the ELIGIBLE guardian set — no longer every registration ever made. Enumeration range-reads the eligibility index bounded by available_until >= reveal_end_block, so registrations that cannot be selected (lapsed ones included) cost nothing at all: 400 lapsed registrations add zero gas. What remains is 360 gas per ELIGIBLE guardian, measured at 40. That term is still treated as constant by the declared model, so the ~25% margin is finite headroom, not immunity — see eligible_set_boundary.
conditions.cancel_measurement: Cancel is measured against a live chain like the two creator phases. An earlier attempt used a keeper gas meter and read ~45% low, because the test fixture injects a mock bank keeper while the real handler sends coins once per active guardian — that under-read shipped two out-of-gas failures. A 32-guardian cancel needs ~2.07M gas (0.207 VEIL at the floor price); the consensus block gas limit is 75M (spec.md Network Configuration), so it is includable with ~36x headroom.
conditions.eligible_set_boundary: Phase 1 begins aborting out of gas once the eligible set grows past roughly 139 guardians at max_shares=2, 154 at 7, and 228 at 32 - the point where 360 gas per eligible guardian exhausts the declared margin. Against the model declared before the eligibility index (250,000 + 5,500 x max_shares) the same boundary sat at 62-79 REGISTERED guardians, so band for band this is a 2.2-2.9x improvement - deliberately NOT quoted as the 5.8x drop in per-guardian cost (2,092 -> 360), because the same re-measurement lowered the declared base by a third and absolute headroom shrank with it. The change of driver is the larger win: the boundary is reached by healthy participation rather than dead registrations accumulating forever, and a lapsed registration no longer moves it at all. NOT a closed problem. Widening the margin is the wrong fix: the creator pays the declared limit, so it taxes every creator today to defer the boundary. The real fix is for the declaration to scale with the eligible count. Query/Guardians already returns every field the predicate needs, but there is no eligible-count query and no server-side filter, so the client must page the registry and apply the predicate itself - the same O(registered) walk, moved off-chain where it is unmetered. A client-model change needing its own plan.
conditions.phase_1_measurement: Swept max_shares 2..32 at bump 100, min_shares = max_shares (so max_shares is the only variable), reveal offset 200 (>= commit timeout 110 + 50 buffer), duration 100. gas_used read from the committed transaction, so ante costs are included exactly as a creator pays them.

request_guardians.basis: full-transaction gas_used from a live 1s-block devnet with 40 registered guardians, all eligible (29 July 2026). Envelope fit: the per-share slope from the band extremes, then the largest base no measured point exceeds.

cancel_secret.basis: full-transaction gas_used from a live chain — NOT the keeper harness, whose mock bank keeper reads ~45% low on this handler
